chunks: He said: Abu al-Tayyib al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Tammar reported to me, saying: I heard Abu Bakr ibn al-Anbari say: I heard Ali ibn Haman recite the following by al-Mazini:

"When I refused to accept from fate all that I abhorred, my reproach against it grew long; I grew accustomed to the touch of hardship until I befriended it, and so the beauty of consolation led me to patience; Familiarity with affliction expanded my heart for it, though at times my chest would feel constricted by it; And my despair of people turned me hopeful for the swiftness of Allah's reprieve, from a source I never knew."
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad the Prophet and his pure family, and grant them abundant peace.
ai.seo_question: What does al-Mazini's poem in al-Amali teach about patience and finding hope in Allah's relief during hardship?
ai.summary: A poetic transmission through a literary chain in which al-Mazini reflects on how enduring hardship with patience transforms suffering into familiarity, and how despair of people leads to hope in Allah's unexpected relief.
